questions.stem: In the sentence 'The tall boy ran quickly.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'boy' names a person, so it is a noun
'tall' describes the noun 'boy', so it is an adjective
'ran' is a doing word, so it is a verb

solution: 'quickly' tells how the boy ran, so it is an adverb.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Wei Jie kicked the ball.', which word is a verb?

explain.why: 'ball' names a thing, so it is a noun
'Wei Jie' names a person, so it is a noun
'the' is an article that introduces a noun

solution: 'kicked' is the action word, so it is a verb.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'She bought a red umbrella.', which word is an adjective?

explain.why: 'umbrella' names a thing, so it is a noun
'bought' is an action, so it is a verb
'She' stands for a person, so it is a pronoun

solution: 'red' describes the umbrella, so it is an adjective.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'I wanted to go out, but it was raining.', which word is a conjunction?

explain.why: 'out' tells where, so it is an adverb here
'wanted' is an action, so it is a verb
'raining' is a verb form

solution: 'but' joins two parts of the sentence, so it is a conjunction.

questions.stem: Which tense is used in 'Mum cooked dinner last night.'?

explain.why: 'cooked' is a past form and 'last night' shows past time
there is no 'is' or 'are' with an '-ing' verb
there is no 'will', and 'last night' is already past

solution: 'cooked' and 'last night' show an action finished in the past.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Ben said that he was tired.', which word is a pronoun?

explain.why: 'said' is a doing word, so it is a verb
'Ben' is a name, so it is a noun
'tired' describes how Ben felt, so it is an adjective

solution: 'he' stands in for 'Ben', so it is a pronoun.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The book is on the table.', which word is a preposition?

explain.why: 'book' names a thing, so it is a noun
'is' is a verb
'table' names a thing, so it is a noun

solution: 'on' shows where the book is, so it is a preposition.

questions.stem: Which tense is used in 'The children are playing in the park.'?

explain.why: 'are playing' is more than the simple present form
'are' is present, not 'were'
there is no 'will' in the sentence

solution: 'are' with 'playing' shows an action in progress now.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Although it was late, Ravi kept studying.', which word is a conjunction?

explain.why: 'late' describes the time, so it is an adjective
'kept' is a verb
'studying' is a verb form

solution: 'Although' joins the two clauses, so it is a conjunction.

questions.stem: Which tense is used in 'She has finished her homework.'?

explain.why: 'has finished' uses 'has' with a past participle, not a simple past form
there is no '-ing' verb in the sentence
the past perfect uses 'had', not 'has'

solution: 'has' with 'finished' is the present perfect.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Ali is taller than Ben.', what kind of word is 'taller'?

explain.why: a superlative would end in '-est' and be used with 'the'
'taller' describes Ali, a noun, so it is not an adverb
'taller' describes a person and does not name one

solution: 'taller' compares two people, so it is a comparative adjective.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'After school, Mei Ling feeds the stray cats.', which word is the subject?

explain.why: 'feeds' is the verb, the action
'school' is part of the phrase 'After school', which tells when
'cats' is the object, receiving the action

solution: 'Mei Ling' is the one doing the action, so she is the subject.

questions.stem: Which voice is used in 'The cake was eaten by the children.'?

explain.why: there are no speech marks or spoken words
in the active voice the children would come first, as in 'The children ate the cake'
'was eaten' is past, not future

solution: The cake receives the action, so the sentence is passive.

questions.stem: In 'Hana's bag', what does the apostrophe show?

explain.why: a plural noun is made with 's' and no apostrophe
direct speech is shown with speech marks
here it is not a short form of 'Hana is'

solution: The apostrophe and 's' show that the bag belongs to Hana.

questions.stem: In 'The pianist played surprisingly beautiful music.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'music' names a thing, so it is a noun
'played' is an action, so it is a verb
'pianist' names a person, so it is a noun

solution: 'surprisingly' describes the adjective 'beautiful', so it is an adverb.

questions.stem: In 'The boy who lives next door is my classmate.', what is 'who lives next door'?

explain.why: it cannot stand alone as a sentence
a conjunction is one joining word, not a whole group of words
it describes the noun 'boy', not a verb

solution: It begins with 'who' and describes the boy, so it is a relative clause.

questions.stem: What type of sentence is 'If I were you, I would apologise.'?

explain.why: it does not order someone to do something
the subject does the action, so it is not passive
it does not ask anything

solution: It says what would happen under an imagined condition, so it is conditional.

questions.stem: Which word is a modal verb in 'You should wear a helmet when you cycle.'?

explain.why: 'cycle' is a main verb
'wear' is a main verb
'helmet' is a noun

solution: 'should' is a helping verb that shows advice, so it is a modal verb.

questions.stem: In 'Neither the teacher nor the pupils were ready.', what type of word is 'nor'?

explain.why: 'nor' does not show place or time before a noun
'nor' links two nouns and does not describe a verb
'nor' does not stand in for a noun

solution: 'nor' joins 'the teacher' and 'the pupils', so it is a conjunction.

questions.stem: Which of these is a complex sentence?
options: It rained heavily and the field flooded.
It rained, and the match was cancelled.
Because it rained, the match was cancelled.

explain.why: this has one clause, so it is simple
this joins two equal clauses, so it is compound
this joins two equal clauses, so it is compound

solution: It has a main clause and a clause beginning with 'Because', so it is complex.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The brown dog barked loudly.', which word is an adjective?

explain.why: 'barked' is a verb, not an adjective
'loudly' is an adverb, not an adjective
'dog' is a noun, not an adjective

solution: 'brown' is an adjective in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The girl sang happily.', which word is a noun?

explain.why: 'sang' is a verb, not a noun
'happily' is an adverb, not a noun
'The' is an article, not a noun

solution: 'girl' is a noun in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Siti draws beautiful pictures.', which word is a verb?

explain.why: 'beautiful' is an adjective, not a verb
'Siti' is a noun, not a verb
'pictures' is a noun, not a verb

solution: 'draws' is a verb in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The old man walked slowly home.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'old' is an adjective, not an adverb
'walked' is a verb, not an adverb
'man' is a noun, not an adverb

solution: 'slowly' is an adverb in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Aunty Lily gave her a gift.', which word is a pronoun?

explain.why: 'gave' is a verb, not a pronoun
'gift' is a noun, not a pronoun
'Lily' is a noun, not a pronoun

solution: 'her' is a pronoun in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The cat hid under the sofa.', which word is a preposition?

explain.why: 'cat' is a noun, not a preposition
'hid' is a verb, not a preposition
'sofa' is a noun, not a preposition

solution: 'under' is a preposition in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Mei Ling likes tea and Ravi likes juice.', which word is a conjunction?

explain.why: 'juice' is a noun, not a conjunction
'tea' is a noun, not a conjunction
'likes' is a verb, not a conjunction

solution: 'and' is a conjunction in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'A bird sang loudly.', which word is an article?

explain.why: 'sang' is a verb, not an article
'bird' is a noun, not an article
'loudly' is an adverb, not an article

solution: 'A' is an article in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'We flew to Penang last week.', which word is a proper noun?

explain.why: 'flew' is a verb, not a proper noun
'week' is a common noun, not a proper noun
'last' is an adjective, not a proper noun

solution: 'Penang' is a proper noun in this sentence.

questions.stem: Which word shows the sentence 'We visited the zoo.' is in the past tense?

explain.why: 'We' is a pronoun and does not show tense
'the' is an article and does not show tense
'zoo' is a noun and does not show tense

solution: The verb 'visited' is a past form.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is 'Close the door.'?

explain.why: it does not show strong feeling
it does not tell a fact
it does not ask anything

solution: It tells someone to do something, so it is a command.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is 'What time does the bus leave?'?

explain.why: it does not tell a fact
it does not order anyone to do something
it does not show strong feeling

solution: It asks for information, so it is a question.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is 'The sea is calm today.'?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
it does not order anyone to do something
it does not show strong feeling

solution: It tells a fact, so it is a statement.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is 'How lovely this garden is!'?

explain.why: it does not order anyone to do something
it shows strong feeling, which a plain statement does not
it does not ask anything

solution: It shows strong feeling, so it is an exclamation.

questions.stem: Which punctuation mark ends a question?

explain.why: a comma separates parts of a sentence
an exclamation mark shows strong feeling
a full stop ends a statement

solution: A question ends with a question mark.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'I will visit my cousin tomorrow.'?

explain.why: 'will' shows the action has not yet happened
there is no 'have' or 'has' with a past form
'will' and 'tomorrow' look ahead

solution: 'will' shows the action is yet to happen.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'The sun rises in the east.'?

explain.why: 'rises' is not a past form
there is no 'was' or 'were' with an '-ing' verb
there is no 'will'

solution: It states a fact that is always true.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'Dad is washing the car.'?

explain.why: 'is washing' shows an action in progress
'is' is present, not past
there is no 'will'

solution: 'is' with 'washing' shows an action in progress now.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'She spoke softly.', what kind of word is 'softly'?

explain.why: 'softly' is not an action
'softly' does not name anything
'softly' describes the verb 'spoke', not a noun

solution: 'softly' tells how she spoke.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Kids love playgrounds.', what kind of word is 'playgrounds'?

explain.why: 'love' is the verb
'playgrounds' does not describe a noun
'playgrounds' does not describe a verb

solution: 'playgrounds' names places, so it is a noun.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The little girl smiled shyly.', which word is an adjective?

explain.why: 'shyly' is an adverb, not an adjective
'smiled' is a verb, not an adjective
'girl' is a noun, not an adjective

solution: 'little' describes the noun 'girl'.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'was reading' in 'Mei Ling was reading when the phone rang.'?

explain.why: the past perfect uses 'had'
'was' is past, not present
'was reading' is more than a simple past form

solution: 'was' with 'reading' shows an action in progress in the past.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'had left' in 'They had left before the rain started.'?

explain.why: 'had' is past, not present
'had left' is more than a simple past form
there is no '-ing' verb

solution: 'had' with 'left' shows an action finished before another past action.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'have lived' in 'I have lived here since 2018.'?

explain.why: 'have lived' is more than a simple past form
there is no '-ing' verb
the past perfect uses 'had'

solution: 'have' with 'lived' links the past to now.

questions.stem: Which tense is used in 'He walks to school every day.'?

explain.why: 'walks' is not a past form
there is no 'will'
there is no 'is' with an '-ing' verb

solution: It states a habit, so it is the simple present.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The girls quietly entered the hall.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'girls' is a noun, not an adverb
'entered' is a verb, not an adverb
'hall' is a noun, not an adverb

solution: 'quietly' is an adverb in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'She hid the present beneath her bed.', which word is a preposition?

explain.why: 'hid' is a verb, not a preposition
'bed' is a noun, not a preposition
'present' is a noun, not a preposition

solution: 'beneath' is a preposition in this sentence.

questions.stem: What is the subject of 'The smiling baby clapped her hands.'?

explain.why: 'clapped' is the verb
'her hands' is the object that receives the action
'smiling' only describes the baby

solution: The subject is the one doing the action, which is 'the smiling baby'.

questions.stem: What is the object of 'Mrs Goh baked a chocolate cake.'?

explain.why: 'baked' is the verb
'Mrs Goh' is the subject doing the action
this is not a single object

solution: The object receives the action, which is 'a chocolate cake'.

questions.stem: Which sentence is in the active voice?
options: The ball was kicked by the boy.

explain.why: this is passive
this is passive
this is passive

solution: The subject does the action, so the sentence is active.

questions.stem: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The storm will break the window.
The window was broken by the storm.
The storm is breaking the window.

explain.why: this is active
this is active
this is active

solution: The subject receives the action, so the sentence is passive.

questions.stem: In 'Ravi is the tallest boy in his class.', what kind of word is 'tallest'?

explain.why: 'tallest' describes a noun, not a verb
a comparative would be 'taller' and compare two
'tallest' describes and does not name

solution: 'tallest' compares one boy with all the others.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'A flock of birds flew over the field.', which word is a collective noun?

explain.why: 'field' is a common noun, not a collective noun
'flew' is a verb, not a collective noun
'birds' is a plural noun, not a collective noun

solution: 'flock' is a collective noun in this sentence.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The red umbrella is hers.', which word is a possessive pronoun?

explain.why: 'umbrella' is a noun, not a possessive pronoun
'is' is a verb, not a possessive pronoun
'red' is an adjective, not a possessive pronoun

solution: 'hers' is a possessive pronoun in this sentence.

questions.stem: In 'Wow! That was amazing!', what kind of word is 'Wow'?

explain.why: 'Wow' does not join anything
'Wow' does not show place or time
'Wow' does not describe a verb

solution: 'Wow' shows sudden feeling, so it is an interjection.

questions.stem: In 'She finished her work quickly.', what kind of adverb is 'quickly'?

explain.why: it does not tell when
it describes the verb, not a noun
it does not tell where

solution: 'quickly' tells how she finished.

questions.stem: In 'We visited the museum yesterday.', what kind of word is 'yesterday'?

explain.why: it does not tell how
it does not describe a noun
it does not tell where

solution: 'yesterday' tells when they visited.

questions.stem: In 'He is afraid of the dark.', what kind of word is 'afraid'?

explain.why: 'afraid' is not an action
'of' is the preposition, not 'afraid'
'afraid' describes 'He', not a verb

solution: 'afraid' describes how he feels.

questions.stem: Which type of sentence is 'Please pass me the salt.'?

explain.why: it does not tell a fact
it does not show strong feeling
it does not ask for information

solution: It tells someone to do something, so it is a command.

questions.stem: In 'Don't touch the wet paint.', what is 'Don't' short for?

explain.why: 'does' goes with 'he', 'she' or 'it'
'did' is past tense
'will' is future

solution: The apostrophe replaces the 'o' in 'do not'.

questions.stem: What does the apostrophe show in 'It's raining.'?
options: a plural form of the word

explain.why: here nothing belongs to 'it'
a plural does not need an apostrophe
speech needs speech marks

solution: 'It's' is short for 'it is'.

questions.stem: Which word is a verb in 'The baby's laughter filled the room.'?

explain.why: 'room' is a noun
'laughter' is a noun
'baby's' is a noun showing ownership

solution: 'filled' is the action word.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The book that I borrowed is overdue.', which word is a relative pronoun?

explain.why: 'book' is a noun, not a relative pronoun
'overdue' is an adjective, not a relative pronoun
'borrowed' is a verb, not a relative pronoun

solution: 'that' is a relative pronoun in this sentence.

questions.stem: In 'We stayed indoors because it was raining.', what does 'because it was raining' tell us?

explain.why: it does not tell when
it does not tell where
it does not tell how

solution: It explains why they stayed indoors.

questions.stem: Which word is a co-ordinating conjunction?

explain.why: 'although' is a subordinating conjunction
'because' is a subordinating conjunction
'unless' is a subordinating conjunction

solution: 'and' joins two equal parts.

questions.stem: Which word is a subordinating conjunction?

explain.why: 'or' is a co-ordinating conjunction
'but' is a co-ordinating conjunction
'and' is a co-ordinating conjunction

solution: 'because' begins a clause that depends on a main clause.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'We might visit Sentosa tomorrow.', which word is a modal verb?

explain.why: 'tomorrow' is an adverb, not a modal verb
'Sentosa' is a proper noun, not a modal verb
'visit' is a main verb, not a modal verb

solution: 'might' is a modal verb in this sentence.

questions.stem: Which type of speech is 'He said, "I am tired."'?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
reported speech has no speech marks and changes the tense
the subject is doing the action

solution: The exact words are in speech marks.

questions.stem: Which type of speech is 'He said that he was tired.'?

explain.why: the subject is doing the action
it does not ask anything
there are no speech marks

solution: It tells what was said without the exact words.

questions.stem: In 'The tired runners finally reached the finish line.', which word does 'finally' describe?

explain.why: 'runners' is a noun, and adverbs do not describe nouns
'tired' is an adjective
'line' is a noun

solution: 'finally' tells when the runners reached.

questions.stem: What job does 'broken' do in 'The broken vase lay on the floor.'?
options: it names a person in the sentence
it shows the time of the action
it joins two clauses in the sentence

explain.why: it does not name anything
it does not tell when
it does not join clauses

solution: 'broken' tells what kind of vase it is.

questions.stem: In the sentence 'Hana taught herself to swim.', which word is a reflexive pronoun?

explain.why: 'Hana' is a proper noun, not a reflexive pronoun
'swim' is a verb, not a reflexive pronoun
'taught' is a verb, not a reflexive pronoun

solution: 'herself' is a reflexive pronoun in this sentence.

questions.stem: In 'You are tired, aren't you?', what is 'aren't you'?

explain.why: it does not show strong feeling
it does not describe a noun
it does not join clauses

solution: It is a short question added to check a statement.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains an adverbial clause of time?
options: After we ate, we washed the dishes.
We ate the food that Mum cooked.

explain.why: this has no time clause
'that Mum cooked' is a relative clause
this has no time clause

solution: 'After we ate' tells when they washed the dishes.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: Because Ravi practised daily, he improved.
Ravi plays the guitar, and his sister plays the piano.
Ravi, who is rather shy, plays the guitar.
Ravi plays the guitar every Friday.

explain.why: this has a dependent clause, so it is complex
this has a relative clause, so it is complex
this has one clause, so it is simple

solution: Two equal clauses are joined by 'and'.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a simple sentence?
options: When the clown appeared, the children laughed.
The children laughed, and the clown bowed.
The children laughed because the clown was funny.
The children laughed loudly in the playground.

explain.why: this has a dependent clause, so it is complex
this joins two equal clauses, so it is compound
this has a dependent clause, so it is complex

solution: It has only one clause.

questions.stem: Which tense is 'had begun' in 'By the time we arrived, the show had begun.'?

explain.why: 'had begun' is more than a simple past form
there is no '-ing' verb
'had' is past, not present

solution: 'had' with 'begun' shows an action finished before another past action.

questions.stem: What kind of phrase is 'in the park' in 'The children played in the park.'?

explain.why: it begins with a preposition
it does not contain a main verb
it does not begin with a relative pronoun

solution: It begins with the preposition 'in'.

questions.stem: In 'Honesty is the best policy.', what kind of noun is 'honesty'?

explain.why: it is not the name of a person or place
it does not name a group
you cannot see or touch honesty

solution: It names a quality, not a thing you can touch.
